hints: Focus on what the orange precipitate in tube Z tells you about the gas arriving from tube Y.
Remember that 2,4-DNPH gives an orange precipitate only with aldehydes and ketones, so Q must be oxidised to a volatile carbonyl compound.
Compare primary, secondary and tertiary alcohol oxidation with warm acidified dichromate(VI) to see which two can form a carbonyl that is swept over by the air stream.
walkthrough:
**Understand the test in tube Z**

The 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine reagent gives an orange precipitate only with carbonyl compounds, aldehydes and ketones. So a volatile aldehyde or ketone must have arrived from tube Y.

Test result:
$$\text{carbonyl} + \text{2,4-DNPH} \rightarrow \text{orange precipitate}$$

**Understand the reaction in tube Y**

Tube Y is warmed with acidified potassium dichromate(VI), a strong oxidising agent. Air carries any volatile oxidation product over into Z. So Q must be oxidisable to a volatile aldehyde or ketone.

**Check the three alcohols**

1 $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ is primary, oxidised first to propanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, which is volatile and gives a positive DNPH test.

2 $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$ is secondary, oxidised to propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$, which is volatile and gives a positive DNPH test.

3 $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{COH}$ is tertiary, it has no H on the C-OH carbon so it is not oxidised by acidified dichromate(VI). No carbonyl forms, so no precipitate.

$$\text{primary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{aldehyde} \rightarrow \text{carboxylic acid}$$
$$\text{secondary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{ketone}$$
$$\text{tertiary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{no reaction}$$

**Conclude the correct combination**

Only 1 and 2 can produce a volatile carbonyl that gives the orange precipitate in Z. This matches the combination of 1 and 2 only.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes all three alcohols. While 1 and 2 do give a carbonyl product, 3 is a tertiary alcohol and is resistant to oxidation by warm acidified dichromate(VI), so it cannot produce the DNPH precipitate.
options.B: Correct because both 1 and 2 work. 1 gives volatile propanal and 2 gives volatile propanone, both are swept by air into Z and both give an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH. 3 correctly excluded as it is not oxidised.
options.C: Incorrect because it includes 3 and omits 1. Compound 3, $(CH_3)_3COH$, cannot be oxidised so gives no carbonyl, while compound 1, propan-1-ol, does give propanal and should be included.
options.D: Incorrect because it includes only 1. Although 1 alone does give propanal and a positive result, it misses that 2 also works. Propan-2-ol is oxidised to propanone, which is also volatile and DNPH positive.
